name: Cast-Colossus
geological_features: Banded atmosphere with metallic compound cloud layers
Orbital debris ring of ice and metal fragments
Magnetic pole anomalies of extraordinary strength
specific_features: Derelict space station in high orbit
description: Cast-Colossus is a brooding gas giant whose atmosphere is laden with metallic compounds that give its cloud bands a distinctive gunmetal grey and tarnished bronze appearance. The planet's toxic atmosphere churns with slow, massive weather systems that take decades to complete their circuits, and a single enormous hurricane migrates between the northern and southern hemispheres in a centuries-long cycle. The orbital rings are unusually dense, composed of ice and metal fragments that create a glittering belt visible from the nearest habitable world.

The planet radiates a sense of immense, indifferent power. Its magnetic field is extraordinarily strong, warping the solar wind into visible structures of charged particles that crackle and spark in the space around it. Approaching vessels must navigate through radiation belts that degrade unshielded electronics in minutes, and the gravitational pull captures and destroys any object that strays too close. The cloud patterns, viewed through filtered optics, have a machine-like precision to their movement that unnerves observers.

A space station in high orbit, the Colossus Watch, was established as a fuel-skimming platform before being abandoned when the radiation levels proved more damaging to equipment than projected. The station drifts in a stable orbit, its hull pitted by particle bombardment but structurally intact. Its automated beacon broadcasts a standard warning on all frequencies, but embedded within the signal is a data packet that does not match any known encoding scheme and was not part of the original beacon programming.

Cast-Colossus represents a vast reservoir of fusion fuel that remains largely untapped due to the hostile radiation environment. Advances in shielding technology may eventually make extraction viable, and several corporations maintain monitoring stations in the outer system watching for the right moment to invest. The anomalous data in the beacon signal has attracted cryptographers and intelligence analysts, though no one has publicly claimed to have decoded its contents.
